quest.title: The Arc of Intellect
quest.description: With the breaking of the diadem, all has come to an end. Head to the main venue and join Kaveh's award ceremony.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: A Parade of Providence: Act III
chapter.title: Gatherings and Partings

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: ...Thank you all for your excellent performance. And that brings this year's Interdarshan Championship to a close!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Finally, it gives me great pleasure to invite our champion, Kaveh, to the stage to receive his award.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Typically, at this point, we would crown our champion with the diadem as well as presenting them with their award.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: However, we have just received word that Kaveh has inherited Sachin's estate, and made the decision to donate it all to charitable causes.

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: Sachin's estate... is getting donated?

dialogues.speaker: Alae
dialogues.text: So much Mora... and he gave it all up?

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Kaveh's generosity will give many struggling families the chance to change their lives for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Of course, without the diadem and prize money to present, this makes the award ceremony a little more concise than expected. Would you like to say a few words, Kaveh? I'm sure many of our audience, like myself, are curious to learn why you decided to give all this wealth away.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm... not entirely sure what I should say under these circumstances. I'm glad to have won, even though I'd say luck played a big part in that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: As for why I want to give the Mora away... I don't support Sachin's views, and I don't want to take his Mora. With a lot of things in life, people need to experience them for themselves. It shouldn't be up to one person to make a judgment on — not him, and not me either.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, this isn't really the time and place for such weighty and complicated topics. So umm... I guess that's all. I'll leave it there, thanks very much.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Oh, Kaveh... just one moment.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: While this is a short-and-sweet award ceremony, we do still have a prize to present you with. Please take this limited-edition Genius Invokation TCG card.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Additionally, your champion status will be logged in your record. This means that the sages will give priority consideration to any future project proposals you submit.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll take the card. But as for project proposals... Eh, forget it.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: In that case, I declare the award ceremony over. Let's give our champion, Kaveh one last big round of applause!

dialogues.speaker: Aissa
dialogues.text: I still don't really get it. That sum of Mora would've been enough for me to live in luxury for my entire life.

dialogues.speaker: Bahir
dialogues.text: That just means you're not strange enough to understand the way that geniuses think. Come on, we've still got the whole Wisdom Gala to explore!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Glad that's over. I think I'm quite good at giving speeches, but this one was just so tiring...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you mean that you're still exhausted from the competition? Honestly, you don't look happy at all... But whatever else happened, you're the champion, you know? Don't you think you should be proud of that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I suppose... *sigh* Oh, wait. Cyno said that he wanted the card, didn't he? And now I have it, right here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're gonna give it to him? But, if it's a rare one, you should be able to make a tidy sum of Mora off it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Why would I do that? It's of no use to me whatsoever — I may as well just give it to him. Could you pass it on to him for me when you next see him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, this is a super big deal. You should do it yourself! Come on, let's go find Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? But I was gonna rest for a while longer— hey, hey, stop pulling my hair!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha looking at, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm still thinking about the Sachin issue. What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, they gave me this limited-edition Genius Invokation card, and I figured you'd have more use for it than I.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...But it's a limited edition. Are you sure you want to give it to me?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What else would I do with it? I have no use for it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But... it's limited-edition... Kaveh, are you in trouble? You don't have to do all this. Just tell me what's wrong, and I will help.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's not what I meant at all! Yes, I have all sorts of problems, but that has absolutely nothing to do with this card. I'll figure my own issues out by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright. In that case, I accept your generosity.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But now that I realize that you have no concept of its value, I cannot simply take it from you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...How about this? I shall buy it from you at a fair price — namely, the price that the previous limited-edition card sold for.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, come on. It's just one card, how much could it really be worth?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: 1 million Mora at the very least.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...H—How much!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A million Mora!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If you feel that's too low, I can go a little higher.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: 1 million Mora for a card!? But you already have a whole bunch of these... uh, shiny ones, don't you? I saw your deck last time we played...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Not every card is this valuable, and some cards are exquisitely designed, but not rare.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh. Well, I guess they must pay you plenty to be General Mahamatra if you're splashing out on things like this...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But really, it's fine. I'd feel bad taking Mora from a friend.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't feel bad. I save a lot. I can spare the Mora for this card.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Uh, you don't spend all your savings on your hobbies, do you? You should watch that, you know... You definitely don't want to end up borrowing money in a moment of impulsivity... Living with debt is miserable.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Sounds like you're speaking from personal experience. I guess you've been through a lot?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...I don't want to talk about it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: In that case, maybe you're the one who should be listening to your advice.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: In any case, I, Cyno, will take this precious card, and it shall join the deck of destiny! Kaveh, come with me in a few moments to collect the Mora. Thanks to you, I have achieved my goal for participating in this tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, if you insist, far be it from me to refuse your courtesy any further. Well... At least I'll be able to keep on top of my bills this month. Maybe I'll even have some left over? In fact, lemme treat you all to a meal later. Bring Tighnari and Collei, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this is what they call "all's well that ends well"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders how the other contestants are doing! Let's go check in with them, shall we? Since we're Guest Commentators and all!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'm telling you, you can't go wrong taking advice from me on what to wear. Back in the day, my fashion style was considered cutting edge by everyone in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Really? Well then, uh, sure... M—Madam Faruzan. Maybe you could pick out a few fashionable outfits for us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faruzan, Nilou... even Dehya and Candace are here! What are you all up to?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Candace and I bumped into these two while we were strolling through the streets.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan here's pretty friendly — when she heard that we were buying clothes, she decided to give us some help.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm... I don't really see anything I'm familiar with. Never mind, we can purchase some textiles and make the clothes ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Let's go with a plain fabric as our base, and embroider red and pink flowers on. Oh, and some green leaves...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... You sure that's the latest style? That sounds a lot like what the older folks back home would wear...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Don't worry, this style is a timeless classic...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Uhhh, no thanks. This is actually sounding pretty weird.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, wait... Madam Faruzan's right, that style is a classic, and used to be mainstream fashion. But these days, there are some other options, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, how about I pick some clothes out for everyone? It's not often that we get to meet up, especially since Candace rarely makes it to Sumeru City. Also, I know a few places where I can get a great bargain!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Sure, I'm happy to leave it to you.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'll come with you to have a look. One always has to keep on top of what the youth of today are into...

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan? ...Come quick, she's over here!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm? Who are you...?

dialogues.speaker: Fawara
dialogues.text: We're new in the Akademiya. We saw all the amazing things you did during the competition... Do you have any classes we could sign up for?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ahem! Of course I do — and you're both very welcome to join.

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: That's great! We can't wait... Um, what's your area of research? Precision mechanics?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: ...I'm from Haravatat.

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: Huh? But you seem like an expert in machines... Wait, sorry, I remember now. You were representing the Haravatat Darshan in the Championship...

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: Their classes are so boring, though! I'm sorry, Ma'am... let me know if you run any other classes in the future, I'll be there!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmph! I knew it... What about you? Aren't you going to leave with your friend?

dialogues.speaker: Fawara
dialogues.text: I think you're amazing, Madam Faruzan, and I'd like to learn from you for a while if possible.

dialogues.speaker: Fawara
dialogues.text: I can take the class you're teaching as an option, even though cross-Darshan lessons might be a little tough to arrange... But I look forward to learning from you!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I see... you're a good egg, child! Don't worry, study under me, and I promise you you will get the best teaching available!

dialogues.speaker: Fawara
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Ma'am. Well, I won't disturb you any further. See you in class!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I don't quite understand what happened there, but... congratulations, I think?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, would you two like to come and pick out some clothes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, we can't. We've got a meal with Kaveh later, and we have to check in with all the other contestants before then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! By the way, have any of you seen Hat Guy or Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I don't know where Hat Guy went... We just saw Layla not too long ago, though.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But she was hanging out with some other Rtawahist students, so we didn't get a chance to speak with her. Are you gonna go and see what she's up to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rtawahist students... They must be the ones who voted for her to enter the competition, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She didn't end up winning, so Paimon wonders how they feel about that. Let's go take a peek.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, everyone. I could have done better in the third round...

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: Oh, stop it.

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: If you're going to beat yourself up after doing as well as you did, how bad does that make us look, huh? Heck, it's not like any of us had the guts to enter the Championship.

dialogues.speaker: Qamar
dialogues.text: I didn't see the whole thing, but you were the only contestant who scored points in both the first two rounds, right?

dialogues.speaker: Qamar
dialogues.text: And I heard that you actually found the diadem first in round three. You came so close to winning the competition!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I just got lucky, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: That can't be true — you had some really stiff competition out there! The renowned Tighnari from Amurta, even Cyno the General Mahamatra was there... You're amazing, all of you!

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: Getting points off them is a huge achievement! The way I see it, people aren't exaggerating one bit with the nicknames they give you. You are a genuine genius!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Thanks a lot. But I really don't think I qualify as a genius... In the second round, for instance, I dozed off and somehow found myself beside the device when I came to.

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: Ah, come on, don't be so hard on yourself. We've decided — we're taking you out to celebrate, and that's final!

dialogues.speaker: Sidra
dialogues.text: Let's go! Cheer up, Layla, the rest of today's all about you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like things are going well for Layla. This is great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't seen Hat Guy since the end of the competition... Oh well, it's almost meal time. We'd better go meet up with Kaveh and Cyno now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Are you sure you have enough to cover this? Don't blow it all at once.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I budgeted very carefully, and this is well within my means. Anyway, I've lost count of how many times you've treated me. It's high time I returned the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, look at all this! Good food, here we come!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I heard that you went to see the other contestants. How's everyone doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faruzan found herself a student, and Layla's classmates are bowled over by how well she did. We couldn't find Hat Guy, though. Who knows where he's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alhaitham's gone missing in action, too. Huh. The one time I'm actually in a good enough mood to treat him to a nice meal, he disappears without a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...That guy... where the heck could he have gone? I still have questions about that note he left...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, whatever. He can do what he wants. Now, let's eat!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You all share a delicious meal...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You shocked me a little when you hurled the diadem to the ground. On further reflection, of course, it made sense, but at the time I was expecting at least some amount of deliberation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Sachin's voice started talking to me inside my head from the moment I picked it up. I could feel his emotions, too... It was a mix of despair and horror swirling around inside my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: He bombarded me with his ideas relentlessly, like he was trying to brainwash me... It gave me a splitting headache that only got worse as he went on.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Like I was saying at the time, his views are not necessarily completely without value, but if all his research does is lead to misfortune, then we're probably better off without it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If his forbidden research were to spread in a harmful form, and cause people to suffer, the matra would step in and ban it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I think you did the right thing. I suppose another way to approach it would have been to claim that you agreed to inherit his research, but give up the research as soon as you've inherited the wealth. But that wouldn't have been your style.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I won't comment on his theories or experiments, but I don't believe that he was careless in his choice of candidate... He chose you. That means he knew what he was doing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Perhaps. I just think that if you accept someone else's things, you should honor their wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: That's a good thing... It means that you have integrity.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Thank you, oh my god, thank you... See, you get me, Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's a good thing Alhaitham isn't here right now... He'd be quick to explain why you're wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Seems like you always include him in the conversation, even when he isn't here...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yep. No dinner with Kaveh is complete without a few words about Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I sense that Alhaitham has in fact been here with us all along...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: He's here? Where!? Why didn't you tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...He lives rent-free in each of our hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That was horrifying. It literally sent chills down my spine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good thing he didn't say that before we started eating. That would've killed the mood in a heartbeat...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, enough about Alhaitham. Tighnari, did you achieve what you wanted out of the Championship?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I did — in the first round, in fact. Word of mouth proved very effective. I spoke to a handful of people, they told their friends, and so on. Now, a record number of people have signed up to attend the next lecture.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, are you free next month? You should come along. Maybe even say a few words.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: About what? I don't know the first thing about anything Amurta-related.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Just play to your strengths. For instance, you could talk about the distinguishing features of rainforest architecture. Or ask everyone not to chop down too many trees the next time they're building a house...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, well that's no problem. Sure, I'll make time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Has everyone had enough to eat? I can order more if anyone's still hungry.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm full, thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's super full too! If only we could eat like this every day, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, we should do this more often. Work will always be there, but seeing friends is important, too. This is a good restaurant. Let's definitely come here again.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sounds good. We should pick a few other places as backup options, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are other good places around here, too? Don't forget to invite us if you go! There's nothing we love more than good food!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Well, it looks like this Interdarshan Championship's a wrap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All that stuff with Sachin and the diadem got sorted, too... Have you still got anything else on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sachin's research...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... Yeah, Sachin said that he'd placed his research materials at somewhere beginning with "A," but Kaveh smashed the Diadem of Knowledge before he could finish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It might be dangerous if someone finds his old research stash, right? "A"... "A"... Where do you think it could be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Aaru Village"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Holy smokes, you're right! He said he spent all that time researching in the desert, didn't he? So it's very possible that that's where he'd leave all his notes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then, let's head off to Aaru Village and try our luck!

talks.objective: Go to Aaru Village and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Didn't expect to run into you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham!? What're you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what are you reading? Are those—

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Sachin's notes. Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I came across his profile while I was organizing some documents, and became interested in his research.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If it wasn't for that, I never would have agreed to being a commentator. I had a hunch after seeing the fragment of his mind, and sure enough, I came here and found his research.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, so you've read it already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright? How do you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I think you may have misunderstood something. The reason Sachin chose that architect to inherit his research was that only he could really empathize with both the calamity and the humanity that these notes seek to convey.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Only one who resonates with these sentiments would suffer, and begin to think of history as bleak, the present as perplexing, and the future as pessimistic.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Empathy is a double-edged sword. Clearly, I am not the same sort of person as Sachin was.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Empaths have many friends, and their wide social circle comes with certain societal advantages. But this also makes it hard for them to achieve their goals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: All important things in life involve other people. As such, it's extremely difficult to live a life that causes no harm whatsoever to others.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If you really want to achieve your goals, you have to be prepared to make enemies along the way. Not everyone can deal with that reality.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And that reality is like the material here... objective, heavy, negative... But at the end of the day, for all these experiment results and conclusions, it's just one person's perspective — Sachin's.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what are your thoughts now that you've read it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As a scholar, Sachin was, without a doubt, a genius.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: He laid the blame for the darkness in the world squarely on humanity, experimented extensively with reliable results, and drew logical conclusions... In that sense, one might say his views were "correct."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... people are bad, and things can only ever get worse? All of that's true?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That is not a question for me to answer. Someone else will arrive shortly — you can ask them instead.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: All I will say is that the world is not built on "correctness" alone. Sometimes, being correct means nothing at all.

choices.text: Those words you wrote among your notes...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: "Lofty ideals may provide no defense at all against nihilism, but perhaps little decisions can."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: "By their own choice, the idealist seeks to bring happiness to all, while denying themselves the same. Thus they shall never reach even the borders of truth until they wipe away the ignorance that blinds them."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I have never been able to agree with certain philosophies. Even Sachin himself struggled to comprehend the notion of sacrificing oneself for the greater good.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: But sadly, all viewpoints will find their supporters, and the way we see the world largely decides our fates.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Alright, then. I got what I came for — these research materials are yours to look after. I'll be off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. So you came here just to read this stuff? You missed out on a big get-together, you know!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: A get-together? ...Ah. Yes, that makes sense. This is a good opportunity for that sort of thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess what? Kaveh treated everyone this time.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Then I'm sure he packed up the leftovers for me. See ya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there he goes... Well, it seems like he really wasn't affected by this research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He said that someone else would answer our questions. Who do you think that'll be?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You wait around near the research materials...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're already here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida... oh, and Hat Guy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you asked him to take part in the Championship?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, it was me. Are you surprised?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you know that there was something wrong with the diadem from the start? And if so, why didn't you switch it out for another one?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Because Sachin's research is not mistaken. He spent his entire life researching this topic, and these materials are a result of that.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: These are the crystallization of his wisdom. Yes, I was worried that the material might cause some disruption, but I didn't want to wipe away all his hard work searching for the truth.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So instead, I had Hat Guy here help me keep an eye on things.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Seriously? I think you can stop calling me that now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Why? Don't you like it?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...*sigh*

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Well, anyway — if Sachin's chosen successor hadn't been able to handle his research, or if it had brought pain to more people, he would have intervened at a suitable moment.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: And after all that, the person Sachin chose, turned his nose up at his life's work. Pretty hilarious.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I was also hoping that this could be an opportunity for you to learn how to interact with people normally... But it looks like that didn't work out.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That wasn't necessary. I'm still paying you back for your help, and the last thing I need is more reasons to be indebted to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida, what did you mean by "Sachin's research is not mistaken"? Does that mean that you approve of his research?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmmm. Put it this way instead. Truth, to me, is like a Shroomboar.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Some people only see the mushroom on the Shroomboar's back, and they conclude that a Shroomboar is a mushroom.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Others see only the Shroomboar's body, and they declare that a Shroomboar is a boar.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Still others look deeper inside, and determine that a Shroomboar is... meat.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: These conclusions are all correct in their own way, but none of them objectively describe the Shroomboar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon kinda gets it... but also not really...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The world is the same way. No one, not even I included, can understand it in its entirety. All of us are somewhere on the path toward truth.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Within the confines of our limited knowledge, some may blindly believe in the beauty of this world, and others may focus only on its evils.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: In truth, the most important thing isn't what state the world is in now, but what people hope it will become. But of course, I don't mean that as a criticism or a call to action.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Ultimately, my duty as the God of Wisdom is to guide every form of wisdom to a place where it can find its purpose.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That was a long speech. So what are you actually going to do with these research materials?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Because Kaveh, as the successor of this research, does not wish to see these ideas disseminated, I will seal it up.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But even though Sachin's research could be considered "negative" wisdom, it is still a building block of the truth. If someone wishes to follow in his footsteps in the future, I will not stop them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I also look forward to the day that a member of the Vahumana Darshan can not only comprehend his theories, but also find a way out from the despair as well.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmph, Vahumana doesn't have that kind of talent... Wait, you're not intending to keep me in Vahumana long-term, are you?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hah, I don't remember signing up to become a scholar. Don't you think I'm useful enough to you as a prisoner?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh boy, here we go again...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You think so? Well, to that, I would say that in Sumeru, even prisoners have the right to an education.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I hope that your studies in Vahumana will help you deal with your own fate, and learn how best to settle old debts from your past.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I will review your final thesis myself. I am expecting great things from you, Mr. Hat Guy.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Tsk.

choices.text: What did that line written in ancient script mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: If you don't come to Sumeru City often, classic floral designs aren't a bad choice. Those don't really go out of style.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: And of course, since you're putting this on your body, you need to consider the type of fabric the clothes are made from. Some materials might look stunning, but they can be terribly uncomfortable to wear...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Agreed. After all, is fashion not the constant phasing in and out of classics? In that sense, you could always consider the style I suggested, too...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait. Sorry, Ma'am, but I think it could be quite a while before the style you recommended comes back into fashion...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I actually think the style recommended by Madam Faruzan is quite beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Isn't it just? You have a discerning eye, my dear!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I can't believe it, but in the end, no one was disappointed in me. What a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Finally, I can get some good sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Since everyone is free, why don't we play a few matches of Genius Invokation TCG?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Eager to show off your new limited-edition card, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Not to show off. This is my way of thanking you for your help. Only my best friend will have the honor of seeing this card's debut play!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, sure. I didn't bring my deck with me, though, so I'll need to borrow one.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Actually, Master, I made a new one a few days back...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Don't tell me you've been spending all your study hours playing cards?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Come on, no need to be so stern. They do say that your innate interests are your best teacher, don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the ceremony will be held at the main venue. Let's head over and check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was thinking of maybe going to the Akademiya for some alone time. Nothing set in stone, though — why do you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: (I think I might need some more practice if I wanted to embroider my own complex designs... Although, I'm no beginner with a needle and thread. More like... upper end of intermediate?)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: (These clothes all seem a bit too flimsy. Is there anything sturdier?)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Dehya and Candace are both pretty tall. That means they have a lot of options when it comes to clothes...)

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: (The classics are the best, period.)

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (I wonder when Kaveh will be able to pay off his debts? *sigh*... I wish him the best of luck.)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: (This was some pretty successful ordering today — not a dish wasted. Oh, I almost forgot, I should order a couple of extra things to take back home...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (It's been so nice not having to study these last few days... I hope I don't fall behind. Hmm... Wait... Uh-oh! I've completely forgotten where I was up to!)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (With this limited-edition card in my deck, I have reached peak connection with my cards. This is my most worthwhile purchase in quite some time.)

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: (What a relief.)
